purpose: Discovery register for potentially useful open industrial-maintenance knowledge and data. It is not an imported fault database.
policy: Do not copy repository contents or datasets into this project until the exact license, dataset terms, attribution requirements, and provenance are checked. Research papers and public GitHub visibility do not by themselves grant redistribution rights. Permissively licensed dataset metadata and candidate snapshots may be stored in isolated research folders with attribution and source evidence; no candidate data is loaded by runtime until separately reviewed and approved.

sources.title: Open-FDD — HVAC fault detection and diagnostics
sources.version: GitHub application release v5.0.21 (2026-11-20); pyproject Python package version 4.5.11 (separate package version)
sources.codeLicense: MIT (LICENSE and pyproject.toml verified; GitHub repository API license metadata currently reports NOASSERTION)
sources.dataLicense: CC BY 4.0 for the LBNL FDD dataset (verified in DOE Open Energy Data Initiative submission 5763 and Data.gov catalog); the Open-FDD fixture README records attribution and transformations. Other datasets/examples remain per-source and are not covered by a blanket license.
sources.licenseStatus: MIT verified for repository code; LBNL dataset CC BY 4.0 verified in OEDI/Data.gov metadata and fixture attribution; GitHub API repository license metadata reports NOASSERTION; no blanket license established for unrelated examples.
sources.contentsReviewed: Reviewed current README, license, Python package metadata, latest GitHub release, generated rule index, SQL rule-pack README, security documentation, LBNL benchmark documentation, fixture attribution, generated FDD catalog and pandas rule runner. The rule index states 78 SQL fault/analytics rules and 72 pandas twins; the standalone PostgreSQL README says 77 registry SQL templates, so the published counts are not identical across surfaces. Rules use Haystack point roles, SI units, confirmation windows and run-proof gates. The SQL/Pandas parity harness uses deterministic synthetic screening data, not field-accuracy validation.
sources.dataOrigin: The broader LBNL FDD collection covers rooftop units, single-duct and dual-duct AHUs, VAV boxes, fan coil units, chiller plants and boiler plants. The Open-FDD benchmark uses eight selected files from the simulated single-duct AHU dataset; the committed two-day fixture is derived from AHU_annual.csv and coi_stuck_050_annual.csv, with subset and rounding documented.
sources.potentialUse: HVAC FDD and SI-unit rule-engine reference; use the LBNL fixture only as an isolated benchmark with attribution. Port an individual rule only after checking its equation, point roles, operating gate, units, parity and asset applicability.
sources.reportedScope: HVAC fault detection, diagnostics and retro-commissioning using SQL/Pandas rules and Normal Framework integration; BACnet/Modbus/Haystack/MQTT field data paths are described in the current project materials.
sources.accessStatus: Current master README, LICENSE, pyproject.toml, VERSION, GitHub release v5.0.21, docs/rules/index.md, sql/fdd/README.md, docs/security.md, docs/ml/lbnl-ahu-benchmark.md, LBNL fixture README, fdd-catalog.json and pandas rule runner fetched and reviewed on 2026-11-25; no code or benchmark execution performed.
qualityNotes: Not a general industrial root-cause knowledge base; scope is building/HVAC FDD and RCx.
Rule index says 78 SQL and 72 pandas twins while the standalone PostgreSQL pack says 77 SQL templates; reconcile version/surface before using counts.
Rules require correct Haystack role mapping, SI unit normalization, operating-mode gates and run-proof; a flag is not a verified root cause.
SQL/Pandas parity tests use deterministic synthetic screening data and do not establish field diagnostic accuracy.
LBNL AHU data is simulated and each selected fault scenario is present for the full year; do not randomly split overlapping time windows.
Benchmark documentation notes byte-identical OA-bias and coil-leakage source archive members; de-duplicate before scoring to avoid duplicated evidence.
Do not infer RUL or causal root cause from anomaly/FDD output alone.
The original OEDI catalog confirms CC BY 4.0 for the LBNL dataset (DOI 10.25984/1881324); this does not extend to unrelated third-party examples or standards.
sources.dataLeakage: LBNL benchmark is simulated and fault labels persist through full-year files. The benchmark notes multiple byte-identical archive members for OA-bias and coil-leakage cases. Use group splits by source file/fault scenario and temporal holdouts; do not random-split overlapping windows or duplicate archive members.
sources.dependencies: Python >=3.11 in current pyproject; openpyxl base dependency, optional pandas/NumPy/SciPy, DuckDB, PostgreSQL/psycopg, RDFLib and reporting/ML extras. Full Normal Framework app and database/edge services are separate from the Python package.
sources.androidWorkerCompatibility: Not a direct Android or Cloudflare Worker dependency. The Python/SQL/Normal Framework stack is too large for the Toolkit runtime; individually reviewed equations may be reimplemented in JavaScript with explicit SI units, input contracts and regression fixtures.
sources.reuseConditions: MIT applies to repository code; preserve LICENSE and notices if code is reused. The included LBNL-derived fixture is CC BY 4.0 with attribution and change notes. Verify each other dataset/example separately; do not treat the repository MIT license as a blanket data license.
sources.originalDataSource: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory / DOE Open Energy Data Initiative (OEDI) LBNL FDD Data Sets, DOI 10.25984/1881324; OEDI submission 5763 lists CC BY 4.0. The Open-FDD benchmark uses the simulated single-duct AHU subset; the broader LBNL collection spans seven HVAC system types and mixed simulation, laboratory and field sources.

sources.title: SCADA-MV-IDS Dataset

sources.licenseStatus: README badge and text claim CC BY 4.0 for the dataset, but no repository LICENSE file was found and the original publisher license was not independently verified in this review.
sources.accessStatus: Git tree, readme.md and docs/labels_mapping.md inspected. dataset/SCADA-MV-IDS.csv.gz is present, but its binary payload was not downloaded or inspected. No LICENSE file is present in the tree.
sources.codeLicense: not declared; no repository LICENSE file found
sources.dataLicense: CC BY 4.0 claimed by README only; pending confirmation from the original publisher and paper
sources.contentsReviewed: Reviewed the repository README and label mapping. The compressed CSV is present but its records, schema and file-level rights were not inspected.
sources.originalDataSource: SCADA-MV-IDS testbed; paper DOI 10.1016/j.future.2026.108458. Publisher page/license not independently retrieved in this review.
qualityNotes: This is an OT cybersecurity attack dataset, not pump, motor or process-maintenance failure knowledge.
Labels distinguish normal and attack events; they must not be translated into mechanical root causes or repair instructions.
The README's CC BY 4.0 statement is not backed by a repository LICENSE file in the inspected tree.
No train/test leakage or generalization audit was performed.
sources.androidWorkerCompatibility: Do not bundle the multi-view compressed dataset in the Android PWA or Worker. At most retain a discovery pointer for a separate OT-security benchmark.
sources.reuseConditions: Do not copy the code or dataset until the publisher's exact license and attribution conditions are independently confirmed; cite the paper DOI if used for research.

All Rights Reserved language blocks general code reuse despite public visibility.

sources.title: Pump Maintenance — Predictive Maintenance Pipeline
sources.potentialUse: Methodology and leakage-audit reference only; not a root-cause fault knowledge source.
sources.reportedScope: README describes the Kaggle Pump Sensor Data set: 220,320 one-minute rows over about 153 days, 52 sensors, labels NORMAL (205,836), RECOVERING (14,477) and BROKEN (7).
sources.licenseStatus: No repository LICENSE file or GitHub license metadata was found. The external Kaggle dataset's exact license was not reviewed.
sources.accessStatus: README, src/load_data.py, src/health_indicators.py, src/anomaly_detector.py, src/classifier.py and src/evaluate.py inspected. The external sensor.csv is not committed and was not downloaded.
sources.codeLicense: not declared; no repository LICENSE file found
sources.dataLicense: External Kaggle Pump Sensor Data license not independently verified
sources.contentsReviewed: Reviewed data-loading, rolling-feature construction, anomaly detection, time-based classifier split and metrics-report code. Raw sensor data and generated result artifacts were not present for independent reproduction.
sources.originalDataSource: Kaggle dataset nphantawee/pump-sensor-data, as cited by the repository README.
qualityNotes: The classifier maps both RECOVERING and BROKEN to one positive class; this is state classification, not root-cause identification.
Only seven rows carry the BROKEN label; most positive labels are RECOVERING.
The classifier uses a time-based split, but feature preparation uses bfill on the time series and on test features, creating a potential look-ahead bias that requires a controlled rerun.
README metrics, including near-perfect AUC claims, were not independently reproduced because the source dataset is not included and its license is unresolved.
The Isolation Forest detects deviations; it does not identify the physical failure mechanism.
sources.androidWorkerCompatibility: Python 3.11+ and scientific Python dependencies are described by README; unsuitable for the Android PWA or Worker runtime. Keep any evaluation isolated.
sources.reuseConditions: Do not copy repository code or download/redistribute the Kaggle data until both code and dataset rights are confirmed. Treat reported scores as unverified until rerun with leakage-safe validation.

sources.title: Awesome Bearing Datasets for Diagnostics and Prognostics
sources.potentialUse: Discovery index for selecting bearing benchmarks; each original dataset must be reviewed separately.
sources.reportedScope: Catalogue covers bearing diagnosis and prognostics datasets including CWRU, XJTU-SY, SEU, HUST and Paderborn; README links detailed descriptions and coverage notes.
sources.licenseStatus: Repository LICENSE is MIT for the catalogue repository. The README directs users to datasets hosted by separate institutions; MIT does not grant rights to those datasets.
sources.accessStatus: README, LICENSE and docs/datasets.md inspected. The repository is a catalogue; no raw bearing signals are included in the inspected tree.
sources.dataLicense: Per-dataset and per-originating-institution; not covered by the catalogue's MIT license
sources.contentsReviewed: Reviewed the catalogue structure and selected dataset descriptions, including CWRU, XJTU-SY, SEU, HUST and Paderborn. No raw signals were copied or downloaded.
sources.originalDataSource: Separate originating institutions and repositories listed in docs/datasets.md; each must be checked at its original publisher.
qualityNotes: A discovery catalogue, not a validated dataset and not a fault-case database.
Fault generation differs across datasets (artificial seeded defects versus natural/accelerated run-to-failure).
Sampling rates, sensors, loads and operating conditions are not interchangeable across datasets.
Data leakage and license conditions must be reviewed separately for every selected source.
sources.androidWorkerCompatibility: Do not package the catalogue or raw signals in runtime. Use metadata for offline benchmark selection only after per-dataset review.
sources.reuseConditions: MIT notice applies to repository code/docs; obtain and comply with the original dataset license and attribution for each dataset.

sources.accessStatus: README, LICENSE and recursive tree inspected. Brick_withFSBrick.ttl (1,609,629 bytes) and three .xlsx files are present; their payloads were not parsed in this review.
sources.codeLicense: MIT for repository material explicitly covered by LICENSE
sources.dataLicense: Not separately verified for the Excel analysis files; derivative ontology rights require review against the upstream Brick BSD-3-Clause license and source attribution

No workbook-level provenance, row-level license or data-quality audit was performed.
The derived TTL may include upstream Brick terms; do not assume the repository MIT notice replaces upstream notices.

sources.title: Hydraulic System Condition Monitoring
sources.potentialUse: Evaluation-method reference for the UCI hydraulic benchmark; not a source of general maintenance procedures.
sources.reportedScope: README describes 2,205 hydraulic test-rig cycles for cooler, valve, pump internal leakage and accumulator labels, using 17 sensor channels and statistical/FFT features.
sources.licenseStatus: No repository LICENSE file or GitHub license metadata was found for the code. The underlying UCI dataset is separately licensed CC BY 4.0.
sources.accessStatus: README, src/evaluation.py, reports/data_manifest.json and repository tree inspected. Raw UCI data are downloaded by script and are not embedded in the repository.
sources.codeLicense: not declared; no repository LICENSE file found
sources.dataLicense: UCI Condition Monitoring of Hydraulic Systems dataset CC BY 4.0 (DOI 10.24432/C5CW21); separate from this repository's code
sources.contentsReviewed: Reviewed the training/evaluation split, metrics protocol and manifest with the original UCI archive URL, byte count and SHA-256. The raw archive was not downloaded.
sources.originalDataSource: UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 447, ZeMA; DOI 10.24432/C5CW21.
qualityNotes: The README's reported metrics are model classification scores on laboratory cycle labels, not causal diagnosis or repair guidance.
The evaluation uses a random stratified 80/20 cycle split; the separate ordered-sensitivity analysis is not the primary final split. Group/temporal dependence across cycles is not ruled out.
The manifest provides archive and file hashes, but raw files were not independently re-downloaded in this review.
The repository code has no declared license; do not copy its implementation.
sources.androidWorkerCompatibility: Python 3.12/scientific Python evaluation is suitable only for an isolated benchmark environment; not for Android or Worker runtime.
sources.reuseConditions: Use the original UCI dataset under CC BY 4.0 with attribution if benchmark data are needed; do not copy this repository's code without a separate license.

sources.contentsReviewed: Inspected the 24-entry catalogue and the lbnl-sdahu manifest: publisher, DOI, CC BY 4.0, SHA-256, file sizes, runs, mappings, transformations and known data issues. Inspected _licence.py: NC/ND datasets require explicit acknowledgement, an append-only ledger, and redistribution is marked prohibited.

qualityNotes: Alpha-stage Python toolkit; not a general multi-equipment maintenance assistant.
Its catalogue contains 24 curated datasets and records checksums, provenance, data transformations and known issues.
The reviewed LBNL SDAHU entry is simulated; known unit/placeholder/duplicate-run issues are explicitly recorded and corrected or excluded.
Published validation reports include small-sample confidence intervals; these are benchmark results, not field-wide guarantees.

sources.title: Hydronic Delta-T Diagnostics
sources.version: 0.1.0 (pyproject package version; no GitHub release verified)
sources.dataLicense: Separate sources: LBNL FCU derivative CC-BY-4.0; Open-Meteo weather data CC-BY-4.0 with free-API non-commercial conditions noted by upstream; synthetic circuit data.
sources.licenseStatus: MIT verified for code. LBNL sample data has CC BY 4.0 attribution; committed Open-Meteo weather CSVs are explicitly described by upstream as fetched from a free API for a non-commercial demo.
sources.accessStatus: README, LICENSE, pyproject.toml, detect.py and lbnl.py inspected; no benchmark was executed in this audit.
sources.potentialUse: Isolated HVAC benchmark and review of operating-baseline methods; do not reuse fixed thresholds as generic equipment limits.
sources.reportedScope: Hydronic heating/cooling delta-T checks for valve, flow, sensor and balancing faults; README claims 52 simulated circuits with 40 seeded fault cases and 12 healthy cases, plus an LBNL FCU example.
sources.contentsReviewed: Inspected the rule implementation and LBNL adapter. The method learns a baseline from the first 28 active days and applies fixed project thresholds; the repository states that most data are simulated and no real building/meter data are included apart from the LBNL benchmark derivative.
sources.originalDataSource: LBNL FDD Data Sets, DOI 10.25984/1881324 (FCU subset); Open-Meteo historical weather API; synthetic hydronic circuit generator.
sources.dataOrigin: Synthetic hydronic circuits, a transformed LBNL simulated fan-coil dataset and Open-Meteo weather CSVs.
qualityNotes: The README's 40/40 seeded-fault results are self-reported and were not independently rerun.
The first 28 active days are assumed to be healthy baseline; a contaminated baseline can bias every later rule.
Fixed thresholds and illustrative tariffs/efficiency assumptions are not universal engineering limits.
LBNL FCU source data are simulated; no independent field validation was demonstrated.
sources.dataLeakage: Do not mix synthetic runs or time windows from the same circuit across train/test. Require separate plant/building validation before generalizing any result.
sources.dependencies: Python package with NumPy, pandas and scikit-learn; not a browser/Worker runtime dependency.
sources.androidWorkerCompatibility: Not suitable as a direct Android/Worker dependency; use only as an isolated reference or independently implemented rule after technical review.
sources.reuseConditions: MIT applies to code. Preserve LBNL CC BY 4.0 attribution. Do not use committed Open-Meteo weather data commercially without resolving the upstream free-API non-commercial terms.

sources.title: Operating-State-Aware Monitoring — UCI hydraulic study
sources.codeLicense: No repository LICENSE or explicit code license found; do not copy or redistribute code.
sources.dataLicense: The original UCI Condition Monitoring of Hydraulic Systems dataset is CC-BY-4.0; this data license does not license the repository's code.
sources.licenseStatus: UCI dataset CC BY 4.0 confirmed at the original publisher. Repository code has no declared license.
sources.accessStatus: README, hydraulic data README, measurement audit, stability/confounding report and check_dataset.py inspected. Raw data files are present in the repository tree but were not downloaded or re-run in this audit.
sources.potentialUse: Reference for grouped validation, operating-state stratification and leakage-resistant hydraulic benchmark evaluation.
sources.reportedScope: UCI dataset 447 with 2,205 cycles, five cycle-level targets and multi-rate sensor streams; research evaluates sensor-family combinations for pump leakage classification.
sources.contentsReviewed: Inspected source and audit documents. The repository reports 1,449 stable cycles, 144 contiguous condition blocks, five grouped split seeds and StratifiedGroupKFold; it explicitly says those blocks are not proven independent experimental runs.
sources.originalDataSource: Helwig, Pignanelli and Schütze (2015), UCI Condition Monitoring of Hydraulic Systems, DOI 10.24432/C5CW21.
sources.dataOrigin: UCI/ZeMA hydraulic test rig raw channel files and profile.txt; not field maintenance histories.
qualityNotes: No code license is declared; code reuse is not permitted by assumption.
The UCI labels describe test-rig component conditions, not root-cause narratives or repair instructions.
The 144 groups are contiguous condition blocks, not confirmed independent physical runs.
Raw data are included upstream, but were not downloaded or independently validated in this audit.
sources.dataLeakage: The study uses StratifiedGroupKFold over 144 contiguous blocks and repeats five seeds. This reduces window leakage but does not establish independence between physical experiments; asset/run/campaign grouping remains necessary.
sources.dependencies: Python 3.11 research environment with NumPy, pandas and scikit-learn; Conda environment documented upstream.
sources.androidWorkerCompatibility: No direct runtime use. Use the UCI source data as an isolated benchmark only; do not port the unlicensed repository code.
sources.reuseConditions: UCI dataset may be reused under CC BY 4.0 with attribution. The repository's code has no declared license and must not be copied.

sources.title: Faaster — Reactive Asset Administration Shell Type 2 over OPC UA
sources.version: 1.0.0a4 in pyproject.toml; no GitHub release tag verified
sources.codeLicense: Apache-2.0 (LICENSE and README badge verified; GitHub repository API metadata reports NOASSERTION)
sources.dataLicense: No separate rights statement verified for vendor AAS JSON examples or the bundled OPC UA Part 12 PDF; no maintenance telemetry/fault dataset
sources.licenseStatus: Apache-2.0 verified for project source code; included vendor sample AAS JSON and standards PDF have no independent per-file reuse confirmation in this review
sources.contentsReviewed: README describes a Python framework mapping AAS V3 models to a reactive OPC UA Type 2 server with HDA, events, MQTT/Modbus integration and X.509/GDS certificate workflows. pyproject declares version 1.0.0a4 and Python >=3.12, while README badge says Python 3.11+; docs/known-gaps confirms this mismatch, MongoDB backend NotImplementedError, unused AMQP URL and legacy interface tests that do not run. Security docs state that without --pki-dir the server exposes a NoSecurity endpoint. The Festo JSON test model was inspected structurally only; it is not fault knowledge.
sources.originalDataSource: No industrial fault dataset. Test fixtures include vendor-branded AAS models (including Festo) and the repository tree includes an OPC 10000-12 specification PDF; the rights and redistribution terms for those assets were not separately established.
equipment: Industrial assets represented as AAS models
sensors and actuators represented as submodels
sources.potentialUse: Architecture reference for mapping AAS identity/submodels to OPC UA address space, HDA, events, PKI and GDS; do not import sample asset files or standards PDFs without separate rights review.
sources.reportedScope: Python framework for AAS Type 2 over OPC UA, historical data access, event generation, MQTT/Modbus extension points and certificate/GDS management.
sources.accessStatus: README, LICENSE, pyproject.toml, security-and-discovery, known-gaps, validation guide, server-security integration test and one Festo sample model inspected on 2026-11-25; no build or test suite executed.
qualityNotes: Alpha/pre-release project; pyproject version 1.0.0a4 and Python >=3.12.
README Python badge says 3.11+ but pyproject and known-gaps require >=3.12.
docs/known-gaps reports MongoDB backend as NotImplementedError, AMQP URL parsed but unused, and legacy interface tests that do not run.
Without --pki-dir, the OPC UA server exposes a NoSecurity endpoint; security configuration must be explicit.
AAS model samples are not maintenance fault evidence; do not infer failure modes from asset metadata.
sources.dataLeakage: No labeled fault or telemetry dataset reviewed; benchmark leakage assessment is not applicable. Sample AAS JSON is model/test data, not a fault outcome dataset.
sources.dependencies: Python >=3.12; asyncua[crypto], cryptography, pydantic, gmqtt, aioamqp, pymongo/motor, basyx-python-sdk, asyncpg and optional pymodbus/UR RTDE.
sources.androidWorkerCompatibility: Not suitable as a direct Android WebView or Cloudflare Worker dependency. It is a Python server/database stack; retain only as an architecture reference unless a separate gateway is justified.
sources.reuseConditions: Apache-2.0 applies to code; retain license and notices. Do not redistribute vendor AAS sample JSON or the bundled OPC UA specification PDF until each file's provenance and license are verified. Do not copy standards text.

sources.title: open62541 — OPC UA C client/server stack
sources.codeLicense: MPL-2.0 for the core library; individual examples may carry CC0-1.0 or MPL-2.0 file headers
sources.dataLicense: No maintenance dataset. NodeSet examples, protocol fixtures and attached research/specification files require per-file provenance; no blanket data license asserted.
sources.licenseStatus: MPL-2.0 verified in LICENSE and README; examples/client.c explicitly declares CC0-1.0. Do not generalize one example's license to the whole repository.
sources.contentsReviewed: README identifies an open-source C implementation of OPC UA client/server; FEATURES documents services, subscriptions, security/authentication and PubSub/MQTT support. CMakeLists sets ANDROID_PLATFORM 24 and version 1.5.10. examples/client.c has an explicit CC0-1.0 header. No maintenance cases or fault dataset were found in the reviewed files.
sources.originalDataSource: No maintenance dataset; this is a protocol-stack implementation. OPC UA normative specification text is separately controlled and is not a reusable fault-knowledge source.
sources.potentialUse: Reference for a separate read-only OPC UA telemetry adapter or isolated Android NDK prototype; require endpoint allow-listing, certificate validation, least privilege and explicit site authorization.
sources.reportedScope: C OPC UA client/server stack with subscriptions, historical access, security policies, X.509 authentication, PubSub and MQTT transport.
sources.accessStatus: README, MPL-2.0 LICENSE, FEATURES.md, CMakeLists.txt and the CC0-marked client example inspected on 2026-11-25; release v1.5.10 identified; no build or Android NDK test executed.
qualityNotes: Protocol transport only; no diagnostic rules, fault taxonomy or root-cause reasoning.
CMake contains an Android platform setting, but Toolkit integration and NDK build have not been tested.
Core code is MPL-2.0; example licensing is file-specific.
Android TCP/IP communication with OT equipment would require the INTERNET permission and a separate network/security design; current Android local-assistant draft does not grant that permission.
sources.dataLeakage: Not applicable to training data; any future telemetry ingestion must retain source timestamp, sensor quality, units, asset identity and provenance.
sources.dependencies: C toolchain and CMake; optional crypto backends and platform-specific plugins; native library rather than JavaScript/Worker package.
sources.androidWorkerCompatibility: Possible separate Android NDK native module after isolated build and security testing; not a PWA library. Cloudflare Worker/WASM viability is unverified and is not proposed for current runtime.
sources.reuseConditions: Retain MPL-2.0 notices and comply with source-disclosure terms for distributed modifications to MPL-covered files. Check each example's header before reuse. Do not copy OPC UA standard text or unlicensed sample assets.
